Standard Operating Procedure

PCB AOI

!Before you start
Note: handle the boards with care, always keep them in an ESD environment.
Swipe left or tap Next to move through the steps. Tap any photo to view it full screen.
1Step 1 of 18 · Start of shift

Open File Explorer, go to W:\23. HTML Tools\AOI Inspection and double-click Start_AOI_Bridge.

2Step 2 of 18 · Start of shift

Open Chrome and go to localhost:8086. Press F11 for full screen.

Check the pills at the top right are green, then click Operator.

3Step 3 of 18 · Start of shift

Pick your name and click Set operator. Your name goes on every report.

4Step 4 of 18 · Start of shift

Phone on top of the light box, pointing down through the gap. USB cable into the PC. Light box on, light box LED off.

On the phone go to Settings › Security and privacy › Auto Blocker and turn it off (otherwise the PC can't control the phone).

Unlock the phone. If it asks Allow USB debugging? tick Always allow and tap Allow.

5Step 5 of 18 · Each board

Click Inspect, then click the order that matches the boards in your hand: PCB ID, Rev and PO.

6Step 6 of 18 · Each board

Stick a barcode label on the board in the same position as on the other boards of this type. Flat and straight. Never over a component or connector.

7Step 7 of 18 · Each board

Click the serial box, scan the label, press Enter.

Boards listed underneath were started but not finished – click one to carry on.

8Step 8 of 18 · Front photo

Board front up on the mount in the light box. It must fill the picture, square, same position as the golden.

Press Space to take the photo. Check it is sharp with no glare, then press →.

9Step 9 of 18 · Back photo

Turn the board over (left–right). Press Space, check the photo, press →.

Bad photo? Press Space again to retake.

10Step 10 of 18 · AOI check

The golden is lined up next to each photo. It must sit the same way round as your board and say Good.

Click Run AgnosPCB inspection. Takes 10–30 s.

11Step 11 of 18 · AOI check

Golden the wrong way round? Click Rotate golden 90° until it matches, then run the inspection.

12Step 12 of 18 · Review

Review opens full screen. Left: your board, yellow box = the detection you are on. Right: golden (top) and your board (bottom), zoomed to the same spot.

Compare each detection. Looks the same? Press → – seen = OK.

13Step 13 of 18 · Review

Real fault? Press ↑, click the fault type and type the component ID next to it on the board, e.g. U4.

Only real faults fail a board: missing, wrong, misplaced, skewed or damaged parts. Dust or a bit of contamination is not a fail.
14Step 14 of 18 · Review

Not a defect but worth noting? Press ↓ and pick a reason.

Fault with no box on it? Click it on the big picture to add it. ← goes back one.

15Step 15 of 18 · Result

Seen them all? Press Space. The board shows PASS or FAIL.

PASS: place the board in the correct cardboard ESD box. FAIL: put it aside for rework and tell your supervisor.

16Step 16 of 18 · Result

The one-page PDF report is saved automatically – nothing to move or rename. Open PDF shows it.

17Step 17 of 18 · Result

Reports are in W:\18. AOI\AOI Inspection Reports: one folder per PCB, one folder per board.

18Step 18 of 18 · Next board

Press Space for the next board and go back to the label step. Repeat for every board.

Pinch or scroll to zoom · drag to pan · double-tap to zoom · × to close
